title: What gets a copy in a shared shop
target: Which parts of a Supermarket Simulator shop are kept in step between players, so a shared shop can be reasoned about when something disagrees.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shared shop with more than one player
A disagreement about what each player sees

steps.do: Expect money, stock and licences to be kept by networked managers rather than by each machine.
steps.because: money, the stock and the licences each have a networked manager of their own (NetworkMoneyManager, NetworkInventoryManager, NetworkLicenseManager)

steps.do: Expect the bakery to be shared as two things rather than one.
steps.because: the bakery's oven and the baker each have a networked copy (NetworkOven, NetworkBaker)

steps.do: Know that a clerk is networked as well as being animated.
steps.because: the clerk has a networked copy (NetworkClerk)

steps.do: Expect fittings and the boxes they arrive in to be shared, along with the interaction that opens them.
steps.because: furniture, the furniture box interaction, floor boxes and the floor box interaction each have networked forms (NetworkFurniture, NetworkFurnitureBoxInteraction, NetworkFloorBox, NetworkFloorBoxInteraction)

steps.do: Expect the shop's glass to have a networked interaction of its own.
Watch customers being shared rather than simulated twice.
steps.because: customers, their transform and the view that follows an NPC's transform are networked (NetworkCustomer, NetworkCustomerTransform, NetworkNPCTransformView)

steps.do: Expect vehicles in a shared shop to be shared as well.
steps.because: a vehicle has a networked component (NetworkVehicleComponent)

steps.do: Remember that the day, the janitor, the market cart and packing are each kept in step too.
steps.because: the day cycle, the janitor, the market's shopping cart and packed order bags all have networked forms (NetworkDayCycleManager, NetworkJanitor, NetworkMarketShoppingCart, NetworkOrderPaperBag)

commonMistakes: Blaming a desync on the wrong thing when several parts have their own copies.
Forgetting that the interaction around an object is networked, not only the object.
Treating the bakery's oven and its worker as one shared thing.
Assuming a customer is only simulated by whoever is closest.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
